test_title: RRB NTPC - UG 2025 (CBT 1) Foundational Full Test - 01
subject: general
question: If 'A & B' means 'A is the father of B' and 'A @ B' means 'A is the sister of B', then which of the following expressions means 'H is the father of M'?
solution:
Family Chart :

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca5a73409ec3dc46f06c16fd8337f1d2a8bc0be41aa06489f6451bc9c281396a.png] 

'A & B' → 'A is the father of B'

'A @ B' → 'A is the sister of B'

Family tree:

1) H @ K @ P & M

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/320df8beeb1d0fa35f55f00052ba544d970e41be221ead2885caa4d47dfabba0.png] 

Here H is the aunt of M.

2) K & H @ P @ M

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3490d46047d8f933e46acfb1826292c59661e9967e5b485dae13cb7684a44a7d.png] 

Here H is the sister of M.

3) M & K @ P @ H

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/320df8beeb1d0fa35f55f00052ba544d970e41be221ead2885caa4d47dfabba0.png] 

Here gender of H is not confirmed so H can male or female.

Thus H is either son or daughter of M.

**4) H & K @ P @ M**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/a8d96688450b10b82fa9953a0a9dbb68b19a4278abdc747812c76821968f69be.png] **

**Here, H is the father of M.**

Hence, the correct answer is **"H & K @ P @ M".**
